subject: Post-demo procurement path and billing cutover window
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@polarishealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: procurement path & billing cutover window

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. The team found the latency/cost profiling very helpful. I wanted to capture a few follow-ups from our side so we can move from trial -> paid without surprises. Can you confirm the items below?

Key asks from Polaris:
- Procurement route: we expect to use a PO (finance + vendor onboarding). Please confirm Redwood's PO process and any required paperwork.
- Marketplace interest: our cloud procurement team prefers Marketplace purchases where possible. Does Redwood support AWS Marketplace purchasing for Dedicated/private deployments?
- Trial conversion criteria: our product team will gate conversion on either 10M tokens processed during the pilot OR 30 active users (whichever comes first). Confirm you can observe these metrics and trigger billing.
- Billing start window: we are targeting to begin invoiced billing in early Oct; need to align on a cutover date and a handoff checklist.

Attached: procurement intake form (PDF) for our finance team to fill out.

Would you (and Ben/Rishi) be able to propose a short MAP (mutual action plan) and an expected billing cutover date by EOW? Also please send any contract/SOW templates we should pre-clear with procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Senior PM, Polaris HealthTech
(sarah.liu@polarishealth.com)

Attachment: polaris_procurement_intake.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement path & billing cutover window

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear asks and the intake form — that helps. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps:

What Redwood supports (short):
- PO / invoiced billing: yes, we support PO-based invoicing for enterprise customers. We require a signed SOW and a PO number routed to billing@redwood.ai.
- Marketplace: Redwood supports AWS Marketplace for hosted offerings. For Dedicated/Private deployments, Marketplace may not cover vendor-managed capacity; we can work with Marketplace listing or direct invoice depending on procurement needs.
- Observability for conversion: we can instrument token counts and active user sessions from the trial, and create an automated trigger to flag readiness for billing.

Proposed MAP & timeline (draft):
1) 9/16 — Redwood sends MAP + draft SOW (attached MAP for visibility).
2) 9/20 — Polaris finance reviews procurement intake and confirms PO routing (contact + expected PO date).
3) 9/30 — Target receipt of PO and signed SOW from Polaris.
4) 10/01 — Billing cutover: begin invoiced billing once trial thresholds verified (or alternate agreed date).

Open questions for Polaris:
- If procurement prefers Marketplace, can we get the procurement team's Marketplace contact to confirm whether the PO will flow through Marketplace or be a direct vendor invoice?
- Any legal or security addenda required before SOW can be signed?

Attachment: MAP-Polaris-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes milestones and acceptance criteria.

Ben / Rishi: can you pick up any legal/finance nuances that we should flag to Polaris? I can own MAP updates and scheduling the SOW review.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0193 | tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

From: Paul Sanders <paul.sanders@polarishealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@polarishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement path & billing cutover window

Tessa / Sarah —

Quick note from procurement: Polaris will be using a PO route for enterprise vendors. High level timeline from our finance org:
- 9/20: procurement intake review complete (we should have the finance approver identified).
- 9/27: expected PO issuance (assuming no additional legal redlines).

Marketplace: finance flagged that if a product is available on AWS Marketplace we can buy there, but Marketplace POs create a different invoice flow and accounting code. Our preference would be to buy via Marketplace only if Redwood can guarantee the same support/SLAs for the Dedicated capacity and if the purchase can be tied to our internal chargeback codes. Please confirm whether the Dedicated deployment can be provisioned via Marketplace SKU or if that requires a direct vendor agreement.

Trial thresholds: product agrees with the 10M tokens OR 30 active users gate. We will provide weekly usage extracts to Redwood. We will also need an explicit definition of "active user" for the trial (e.g., at least one session with >5 queries in a 7-day period).

If PO issuance slips beyond 9/27, can Redwood accept a soft start where we begin usage while paperwork completes and backdate billing once the PO is received? That would help the product team avoid a hard stop for the pilot.

Thanks,
Paul Sanders
Head of Procurement, Polaris HealthTech
paul.sanders@polarishealth.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Sanders <paul.sanders@polarishealth.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement path & billing cutover window

Paul / Sarah —

Thanks for the clarity, and helpful to have procurement timeline. A few clarifications and a concrete proposal to avoid delays:

1) Marketplace vs PO
- Dedicated/private deployments: marketplace SKUs generally cover hosted/managed offerings. For Dedicated or on-prem/private packages we typically do a direct vendor agreement + PO because provisioning requires config work and capacity reservations.
- If Polaris can procure a hosted SKU on AWS Marketplace that meets your needs, we can map the chargeback code; otherwise PO via direct invoice is the recommended path.

2) Soft start / backdating
- We can accommodate a soft start: allow the pilot to run immediately and, if PO arrival is delayed beyond 9/27, backdate invoices to the agreed billing start date. We will need a written confirmation from Polaris finance that a PO will be issued and an expected PO number once available.

3) Trial measurement & acceptance
- We will instrument: token count, unique active user sessions, and a dashboard snapshot weekly.
- Proposed acceptance definitions (please confirm):
  • Active user = user who issues >=1 API call in a 7-day window (we can tighten to >5 queries if you prefer).
  • Conversion trigger = first day either 10,000,000 tokens processed during the pilot or 30 active users is observed and validated by both teams.

4) Proposed billing cutover date
- To provide buffer for PO processing and SOW finalization, propose billing cutover = 2026-10-05. That gives Polaris until 9/30 to route PO and until 10/04 for any last-minute SOW updates. If PO arrives earlier we can backdate billing to 10/01 on request.

Next steps (owner):
- Polaris: confirm PO route and whether Marketplace is preferred — include Marketplace procurement contact if so (owner: Paul).
- Polaris: confirm active user definition (owner: Sarah).
- Redwood (Ben): prepare final SOW for signatures and send DocuSign link.
- Redwood (Tessa): update MAP and lock billing cutover date to 2026-10-05 unless we hear an earlier PO.

Docs attached: draft SOW (sow-polaris-draft.docx). HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
DocuSign (pending): https://docusign.com/ABC123-SOW

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if you want to close the PO path quickly.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0193 | tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
